title: Defects, performance claims and referrals
audience: Trainees, workers and quoting staff on the solar panel cleaning track who speak with customers about defects, output and warranties. This lesson does not authorise energy-output testing or system certification.
learningOutcomes: Separate a cleaning observation from a defect finding, a performance claim and a warranty statement.
Record a defect in writing and refer it to the correct person, without certifying the system.
Explain why accreditation references must be current, including the scheme that now applies (Solar Accreditation Australia, per the NSW government page).
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: NSW Government, Installing solar panels (last updated 19 October 2026); Energy Safe Victoria, Safely installing photovoltaic (PV) systems (reviewed 15 April 2025); NSW Government, Building and trades licences and credentials: electrical (last updated 23 June 2026).

instruction.heading: Observation, defect and claim
instruction.body: A cleaning worker may observe that a panel is dirty, cracked, discoloured or loose. Recording that observation is part of the job. Calling it a defect that affects the array's output, or saying that the array will produce more or less power after the clean, is a different statement. Energy-output testing and performance claims are outside this course, and a worker does not make them. Keep the observation, the defect and any claim separate in your record.

instruction.heading: Performance claims
instruction.body: Customers often ask whether a clean will increase energy output, by how much, or whether the inverter reading is correct. The cleaning course does not include energy-output testing, system servicing or inverter checks. The correct response is to say that output claims and system checks are outside the cleaning scope, and to refer the customer to the installer or a suitably qualified person. Do not quote a percentage, a generation figure or a return on investment.

instruction.heading: Recording and referring defects
instruction.body: Record each defect in writing with a dated photograph, its position on the array, and what you observed. Give a copy to the owner. Refer electrical defects, such as burnt or exposed components, to a licensed electrician. Refer equipment or installation defects, such as a loose mounting, to the installer or the array owner. Refer warranty questions to the manufacturer or installer. Keep the referral and the outcome on the job record.

instruction.heading: Accreditation references
instruction.body: Where an installer's accreditation is relevant to a referral, check the current scheme. NSW government guidance (last updated 19 October 2026) says rebate eligibility depends on accreditation with Solar Accreditation Australia, which is the scheme the page names. Do not describe CEC accreditation as current, and correct any older document that does.

instruction.heading: What a worker must not do
instruction.body: A cleaning worker must not certify that an array is compliant, safe, performing or under warranty. The worker must not isolate the system, change settings or repair a defect. The worker must not promise a result for a defect that a licensed person has not assessed. These statements are reserved to the licensed or accredited person or the manufacturer.

instruction.heading: Licence and authority boundary
instruction.body: Licence notice: This lesson does not grant an electrical licence, solar installation licence, accreditation, energy-output certification or warranty authority. Victorian guidance treats PV installation and maintenance as electrical installation work. New South Wales electrical wiring work, including repairing, needs a licence or certificate (page last updated 23 June 2026).

instruction.body: Official sources for this lesson (end): NSW Government (nsw.gov.au), Installing solar panels (page date: Last updated 19 October 2026); Energy Safe Victoria, Safely installing photovoltaic (PV) systems (page date: Reviewed 15 April 2025); NSW Government (nsw.gov.au), Building and trades licences and credentials: electrical (page date: Last updated 23 June 2026).

procedure: Record each observed condition separately from any defect finding or claim.
If a customer asks about output, output claims or inverter readings, record the request and state that it is outside the cleaning scope.
Photograph each defect with its position on the array and record the date and the time.
Refer electrical defects to a licensed electrician, equipment or installation defects to the installer, and warranty questions to the manufacturer or installer.
Check the current accreditation scheme before naming any installer accreditation in a referral.
Give the owner a written copy of the defect record, and record the referral and the outcome.
Do not certify, promise or quote a result for any defect that a licensed or accredited person has not assessed.

workedExamples.situation: A customer asks the worker to confirm that the clean will bring the system back to its original output, and to write a letter saying so.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What can the worker say and write?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not write the letter or give an output promise. Say that output and system performance checks are outside the cleaning scope, and refer the customer to the installer or a suitably qualified person. Record the request and the referral. The cleaning record may describe the work done and the observed condition only.

workedExamples.situation: During a clean, a worker sees a loose mounting bracket on the end of a row and a burnt connector nearby.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How should the two observations be recorded and referred?
workedExamples.reasoning: Record the loose bracket and the burnt connector separately, with photographs and positions. Refer the burnt connector to a licensed electrician, and refer the loose bracket to the installer or array owner. Do not touch the connector or tighten the bracket. Tell the owner in writing and record the referral.

equipmentAndPpe: Defect record template with fields for observation, defect, claim and referral
Camera or phone for dated photographs with positions
Referral letter template for electrical, installation and warranty questions
PPE as specified in the job pack

commonErrors.error: Telling a customer the clean will restore output.
commonErrors.prevention: Say that output claims are outside the cleaning scope, and refer the customer.

commonErrors.error: Describing a CEC accreditation as current.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the current scheme. The NSW government page names Solar Accreditation Australia for rebate-linked accreditation.

commonErrors.error: Tightening a loose bracket or touching a burnt connector.
commonErrors.prevention: Record and refer. Do not repair.

commonErrors.error: Mixing an observation with a warranty opinion in the record.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep observations, defects, claims and referrals in separate fields.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The NSW government page names Solar Accreditation Australia for rebate-linked installer accreditation (last updated 19 October 2026).
Energy-output testing, system servicing and inverter checks are outside this course, and output claims are not made by a cleaning worker.

Licence notice: This lesson does not grant an electrical licence, solar installation licence, accreditation, energy-output certification or warranty authority. Victorian guidance treats PV installation and maintenance as electrical installation work (reviewed 15 April 2025). New South Wales electrical wiring work, including repairing, needs a licence or certificate (last updated 23 June 2026).

qualityStandard: Observations, defects, claims and referrals are recorded separately.
No output, warranty, compliance or safety certification is given by a worker.
Each defect is photographed, positioned and referred to the correct person in writing.
Accreditation references are current, and no CEC accreditation is described as current.
documentationEvidence: Defect record with observation, photograph, position and date
Written referral to the correct person, with the outcome
Record of any customer request for output or warranty statements, and the response
summary: Keep observations, defects, performance claims and warranty statements separate.
Refer electrical defects to a licensed electrician and warranty questions to the manufacturer or installer.
Do not promise output or certify the system.
Solar Accreditation Australia is the accreditor named on the NSW government page.

knowledgeChecks.question: A customer asks whether the clean will increase energy output by a set percentage. What should the worker do?
options: State that energy-output claims are outside this course and not offered
Promise the percentage, since the clean will clearly improve the output
Say the clean will double output on the array and the inverter too today
Quote the estimate from the internet for this roof and this array today

knowledgeChecks.question: A cracked module is found. What is the correct action?
options: Say nothing about it to the owner or the agent at all today
Record it in writing with photos, and report it to the owner
Quote a replacement for the cracked module and the frame today
Replace the module with a spare from the van at once today

knowledgeChecks.question: Which body does the NSW government installing-solar page name for rebate-linked installer accreditation?
options: The Clean Energy Council
Standards Australia
Solar Accreditation Australia
Energy Safe Victoria only

knowledgeChecks.question: A defect looks electrical. Who is the correct referral?
options: The worker's friend who knows about panels and the wiring too
A cleaning company that offers repairs too in the local area
No one, since it is not your problem to solve or report today
A licensed electrician or the installer, as the owner directs

knowledgeChecks.question: Which statement is correct about warranty in a defect report?
options: The worker records observations and refers warranty questions to the manufacturer or installer, without certifying
The worker certifies the warranty is void for the array, the panels and the inverter on the site today
The worker certifies warranty is valid for the whole array, the panels and the inverter at the site
The worker deletes the warranty note from the file before the handover is signed by the customer today
